approach: Test-side changes in crates/athena-cap-study/src/rules.rs: replace the firstmate-only constants (STUDY_SHA, study_dir(), mounted_tree(), STUDY_FILES) with a per-directory entry point `check_study(dir, pin_env, mount) -> Vec<String>` and `check_studies(root, pin_env, mount)` that walks every `studies/*/`. The kept test reads ATHENA_PIN_URL and ATHENA_PIN_SHA from the process environment and passes them in as arguments, so tests never set env vars (the workspace denies unsafe_code). For every directory it checks the conventions (no placeholders, 40-hex pin, every source SHA equals the pin via the existing `wrong_sha` rule with a `NoTree` lookup, every claim text starts `[mechanism]` or `[prose-only]`, a "none" guard is never code-evaluated and has no counters, pin/validation study_id equals the directory name). Only when the pin's URL and SHA equal the env pair and a `pinned-source/` mount exists does it run `validate()` and require `computed == validation.json`. A pin with the same URL but a different SHA fails naming the study id. Fault tests run on tempfile copies; a tree rebuilt from each study's own citations lets the full-validation route run in a plain checkout. `Study::admit` in lib.rs also refuses a change spanning two `studies/<id>/` directories and any path outside one study directory and CHANGELOG.md. The study producer prompt states the conventions, rewritten so the study set grows by no more than 25 tokens (about 75 bytes net), which keeps it at or under the current largest producer set (1043) so docs/system-facts.md, which is not a deliverable, stays untouched. xtask/tests/policy.rs gets `boundary_scan_file(path, text)`, which blanks only claim-source `quote` values in `studies/<id>/claims.json` before word matching and always matches machine-path fragments on the raw text. Planted terms are split strings joined at run time. A CHANGELOG entry is added and `tempfile` becomes a dev-dependency of the study crate.

decisions.choice: Pass the pin env pair and the mount path to `check_study` as arguments; only the kept test reads `std::env::var`.
decisions.reason: The workspace sets `unsafe_code = "deny"` (Cargo.toml line 59), so tests cannot call `set_var`. Arguments let temp-copy tests exercise every pin case in parallel without touching process state.

rejected.why: Needs unsafe in edition 2024 and races with parallel tests.

rejected.option: Run a child `cargo test` with env set
rejected.why: Slow, and the verifier may run only whole simple cargo commands.

decisions.choice: Reuse the existing `wrong_sha` rule (rules.rs:264), run with a `NoTree` GitLookup that answers nothing, as the check for a source SHA that differs from the pin. The offending id is the owner id the rule already reports (claim or card id).
decisions.reason: `wrong_sha` only compares strings and never calls git, so it works with no tree. This avoids a second SHA comparison that could drift.

rejected.option: Re-implement the SHA comparison in the test
rejected.why: Duplicates logic that can drift from the rule.

decisions.choice: Put the convention checks in the `#[cfg(test)]` module of rules.rs, as the kept test is today; `RULES` (18 rules) is unchanged.
decisions.reason: The request names the kept test in rules.rs. The conventions are repository policy over study data, not part of the validation core, and adding rules would change validation.json for firstmate, which may not change.

rejected.why: This would change firstmate's validation.json, and nothing under studies/firstmate-work-handling/ may change.

decisions.choice: With no mount, env unset, or env naming another URL, check conventions only. With env naming the pin's URL and SHA but no mount, conventions only. With env naming the pin's URL and a different SHA, fail naming the study id whether or not a mount exists.
decisions.reason: This is the request's rule. A mismatch is a fault in pin.json or in the pinning, never a reason to validate quietly against the wrong tree.

rejected.option: Validate any mounted tree against every study
rejected.why: A second study would fail its own quote checks against firstmate's tree.

decisions.choice: Admission: collect `studies/<id>/...` ids over all non-build-output paths. More than one id gives one `study-one-directory` violation naming the ids. Every path that is not build output, not exactly `CHANGELOG.md` at the root and not under `studies/<id>/` gives a `study-outside-directory` violation. Paths with `.`, `..` or empty segments, and a bare `studies/<name>` file, count as outside.
decisions.reason: Matches the brief. Build-output paths keep their existing single `build-output` violation, so `build_output_is_refused` (lib.rs:187) still sees exactly one violation.

rejected.option: Also flag build output as outside the directory
rejected.why: Gives two violations for one path and breaks the existing test.

rejected.option: Allow `studies/README.md` or files directly under studies/
rejected.why: They belong to no study id, and the brief says exactly one directory.

decisions.choice: The boundary exemption blanks only the string values of `sources[].quote` of the claims, and only in `studies/<id>/claims.json` (exactly one id segment). It parses with serde_json to collect the claim quote strings, then replaces `"quote": <literal>` pairs whose literal is in that set, keeping line numbers. Word matching runs on the blanked text, fragment matching on the raw text. If the file does not parse, nothing is exempt. `boundary_scan` stays unchanged so `the_admission_scan_finds_what_the_policy_scan_finds` compares like with like.
decisions.reason: Exempts only text quoting studied source, keeps scanning prose and machine-path fragments.

rejected.option: Skip all of claims.json, or all of studies/
rejected.why: Would hide a claim's own prose and the rest of the study.
The request names the claims' quote fields; rationales.json stays fully scanned. Raised as a user question.

decisions.choice: Revision (finding 2): do not touch docs/system-facts.md. Write the study producer prompt so the study set grows by at most 25 tokens over its current 1018 (the brief's 182 tokens of headroom under 1200), i.e. stays at or under the largest producer set of 1043 recorded in docs/system-facts.md line 23. Do it by tightening existing bullets while adding the three conventions and the one-directory rule. `computed_rows()` in crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs takes the maximum over capabilities, so a study set at or under 1043 leaves the recorded row unchanged.
decisions.reason: docs/system-facts.md is not among the deliverables, so editing it would widen the scope. The size is checkable: `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` fails if the largest set moves.

rejected.option: Update the `- budget producer:` line in docs/system-facts.md when the set grows
rejected.why: The file is not a listed deliverable (finding 2); the plan instead keeps the study set within the existing figure.
The facts file says to update the line, never the budget.

rejected.option: Drop the one-directory rule from the prompt
rejected.why: Admission refuses such changes, so the producer should be told the rule; it is a short bullet.

decisions.choice: Revision (finding 1): the demonstration of criterion 6 states what fails without the behavior: any new lint warning or unformatted line in the added test code.
decisions.reason: Behavior criteria need a fails_without; the check's failure mode is a non-zero exit from the two whole commands.

rejected.option: Leave criterion 6 as a non-behavior seam note
rejected.why: The brief types it [behavior], and the review required fails_without.

`admit()` also refuses a change spanning more than one studies/<id>/ and any path outside one study directory and CHANGELOG.md (build output keeps its own violation); add unit tests.

State the conventions: enforcement tags, no placeholders, a 'none' guard never checked by code, one studies/<id>/ plus CHANGELOG.md per job; tighten existing bullets so the study set grows by at most 25 tokens.

steps: rules.rs, test module: remove `STUDY_SHA`, `study_dir()`, the firstmate-only `mounted_tree()` and `STUDY_FILES` as a fixed list (derive the file list from `studies/<dir>/`). Add `NoTree` (a GitLookup answering None/false), generalize `MountedTree::new(sha, root)`, and add `Loaded::read(dir) -> Result<Loaded, String>` (pin, claims, rationales, model, findings, validation) with `violations(git, rule)` and `validate(git)`.

rules.rs: add `conventions(dir, loaded) -> Vec<String>`. It checks: no 'UNRESOLVED' or 'not examined' (case-insensitive) in any study file; pin.sha is 40-hex; `wrong_sha` (via `NoTree`) reports no owner; every claim text starts '[mechanism] ' or '[prose-only] '; every transition with guard 'none' has `guard_evaluated_by != Code` and empty `guard_counters`; pin.study_id and validation.study_id equal the directory name; each file source has a non-blank quote. Every message starts with the offending id (claim, card, transition or study).

rules.rs: add `check_study(dir, pin_env: Option<(&str,&str)>, mount: Option<&Path>) -> Vec<String>` and `check_studies(root, pin_env, mount)`, which sorts and walks directories under studies/ and fails if there are none. Rules: conventions always; if the env url equals pin.repository_url and the sha differs, a problem naming the study id and both SHAs; if url and sha equal and a mount exists, run `validate()` with `MountedTree`, report each failing rule with its offending ids, and report when `computed != validation.json`. The kept test `every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates` reads the two env vars (non-empty), uses `../../pinned-source` if it is a directory, calls `check_studies` on `../../studies`, and prints which studies were fully validated.

rules.rs: add `synthetic_tree(&Loaded) -> TempDir` (a file per cited path, each quote at its start line, blank lines otherwise) and the tests: `the_study_matching_the_pin_validates_against_a_tree_rebuilt_from_its_citations`, `a_study_that_breaks_a_convention_or_its_pin_fails_naming_the_id` (copy helper, JSON edits, four faults, control, conventions-only case), `a_second_study_directory_is_checked_too`, and ports of the quote, SHA and range mutation checks from the old firstmate test using ids read from the data instead of the literals c1 and ra1.

lib.rs: add `fn study_dir_of(path) -> Option<&str>` (a `studies/<id>/<rest>` path whose segments are all plain, with a non-empty id and rest) and extend `admit()`. Build-output paths produce `build-output` as before and are skipped by the new checks. More than one id gives one `study-one-directory` violation naming the ids. Each other path that is not `CHANGELOG.md` and not under a study directory gives a `study-outside-directory` violation with its path. Add tests for the six cases in the criterion 3 demonstration (keep `build_output_is_refused` as is).

xtask/tests/policy.rs: split `boundary_scan` into `scan_words` and `scan_fragments` (keeping `boundary_scan` as their union, so the admission-agreement test is unchanged). Add `claim_quote_exempt(path)` (exactly `studies/<one id>/claims.json`), `without_claim_quotes(text)` (serde_json parse, collect `sources[].quote` strings, regex-replace `"quote": <literal>` for those literals with an empty string, one line in and one line out) and `boundary_scan_file(path, text)` (words on the blanked text, fragments on the raw text). Use it in `athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where`. Add tests for each case in the criterion 4 demonstration, planting the word and the fragment with `.concat()` from split parts. Grep the file for the banned words before finishing.
crates/athena-cap-study/Cargo.toml: add `tempfile.workspace = true` under [dev-dependencies]. Cargo.lock: add "tempfile" after "serde_json" in the athena-cap-study entry.

producer.md: rewrite with the existing rules kept and these added: start every claim text with `[mechanism]` or `[prose-only]`; give the full pinned SHA; no placeholders (UNRESOLVED, not examined); a guard that does not exist is `none`, never checked by code; change only one `studies/<id>/` and CHANGELOG.md. Offset the additions by tightening: shorten the intro to one clause, drop '(read-only)', merge the tag rule into the claim bullet, shorten the rationale-card, `contradicts` and boundary bullets. Net growth must stay within about 75 bytes of the current 1019. Avoid the word list in policy.rs and the text 'agent-reference'. Then run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets`; it must pass with docs/system-facts.md unmodified. If it fails reporting a larger producer value, tighten further and rerun. Do not edit docs/system-facts.md.
CHANGELOG.md: add the entry under [Unreleased] / ### Changed, without writing the banned words.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked` (or the crate tests named in the demonstrations). Where pinned-source/ and ATHENA_PIN_* are present, confirm the log shows firstmate fully validated. Run `git status` to confirm nothing under studies/, no athena.toml and no docs/system-facts.md changed.

risks.risk: The ATHENA_PIN_* variables may not reach the test process, so full validation would silently not run, which is weaker than today's behavior of validating whenever pinned-source/ exists.
risks.mitigation: The kept test prints which studies were fully validated and which were convention-only. The hermetic test (tree rebuilt from citations) runs the full-validation route in every checkout. The Host open question asks.

risks.risk: The reconstructed tree is built from the study's own citations, so it cannot show that the real tree holds the quotes.
risks.mitigation: The test's doc comment says so. Only the mounted-tree path proves the quotes; criterion 1's mounted case covers it.

risks.risk: The rewritten study prompt grows past 1043 tokens, the recorded largest producer set, and `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` fails; docs/system-facts.md is not a deliverable so it cannot be edited.
risks.mitigation: Step 8 sets a budget of about 75 bytes net growth over the current 1019 bytes, achieved by merging the placeholder rule into one short bullet, dropping '(read-only)', shortening the intro, the rationale-card bullet and the last bullet, and folding the tag rule into the claim bullet. The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` after each edit and tightens until it passes with the facts file unchanged. If it cannot fit, the producer stops and reports it (third open question) instead of editing the facts file.

risks.risk: Study jobs that legitimately touch another path (for example a shared doc) are now refused. The brief expects about 5% newly refused readings.
risks.mitigation: The violation detail names the allowed set (one studies/<id>/ plus CHANGELOG.md) so the producer can fix the change in one retry; the prompt now states the rule.

risks.risk: A studied system's words in a rationale-card quote, or in a claim's own prose, still fail the boundary scan.
risks.mitigation: That is what the request asks for: only claim quotes are exempt. Raised as a user question.

risks.risk: A claim quote that spans lines, or two sources whose ranges collide, could make the reconstructed tree ambiguous.
risks.mitigation: The helper writes each quote at its start line and panics naming the claim id if two quotes cannot be placed, instead of passing silently; the firstmate data was grepped for escaped newlines before planning.

demonstrations.method: Run the study crate tests. The kept test `every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates` calls `check_studies(studies root, env pair read from ATHENA_PIN_URL/ATHENA_PIN_SHA, mount ../../pinned-source if it is a directory)`. A second test `the_study_matching_the_pin_validates_against_a_tree_rebuilt_from_its_citations` passes each study's own URL and SHA as the env pair and a temp tree rebuilt from the study's citations as the mount. A third, `a_second_study_directory_is_checked_too`, builds a temp studies root holding the firstmate copy and a renamed copy with an untagged claim.
demonstrations.observes: With no ATHENA_PIN_* set, every studies/*/ passes the conventions and the test passes. With the pin env set and firstmate mounted, the test runs `validate()` and asserts it equals studies/firstmate-work-handling/validation.json, and prints which study was fully validated. The hermetic test shows the same equality in a plain checkout from a tree rebuilt from the study's own citations (it exercises the route and the recorded equality, not that the real tree holds the quotes). The second-directory test fails naming the second directory and its claim id.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the loop skipped a directory, the second-directory test would not name the bad claim. If the matching branch never called `validate()`, the hermetic equality test would not run validation and compare it with validation.json (a tampered validation.json copy would pass).
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `validate()` and the rules exist (rules.rs). New test-module functions `check_study`, `check_studies`, `Loaded::read(dir)` and `synthetic_tree(&Loaded) -> TempDir` are added by plan steps 1-4. Fixtures: the real studies/ directory, `tempfile::TempDir` copies, and a `MountedTree` over a real or synthetic root (MountedTree exists in the rules.rs test module); root and env pair are injected as arguments. The doubles hold no rule logic: validation, `wrong_sha` and the conventions run the real code.

demonstrations.method: The test copies the first study directory into a TempDir (copy helper, step 4), edits its JSON with serde_json and calls `check_study`. (a) Set claims[0].text to untagged prose: a problem containing that claim id and 'enforcement'. (b) Set transitions[0].guard to "none" and guard_evaluated_by to "code": a problem naming the transition id. (c) Set claims[0].sources[0].sha to a different 40-hex: a problem naming the claim id. (d) Leave the copy unchanged and pass an env pair with the pin's URL and a different SHA, with a temp dir as mount: a problem naming the study id and both SHAs. A control (unmodified copy) returns no problems; a last case (env unset, a changed quote) returns no problems, showing conventions only.
demonstrations.observes: Four asserts of the form `problems.iter().any(|p| p.contains(<id>))` plus the control returning empty. Failure strings begin with the offending id (claim, transition or study).
demonstrations.fails_without: If the tag check, the none-guard check, the SHA check or the pin-mismatch check were removed, the matching case would return an empty list and its assertion would fail. If a message omitted the id, `contains(id)` would fail.

The pin env pair and mount are injected as arguments. The conventions run the real `wrong_sha` rule with a `NoTree` lookup (added in step 1) that only supplies absent git answers.

demonstrations.observes: `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` and `every_role_set_is_within_its_budget` pass, and `git diff --stat` lists no docs/system-facts.md, so the study producer set is at or under the recorded largest (1043 of 1200) after adding the conventions. `cargo test -p athena-context` (test at crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs:652) still passes: no 'agent-reference' in the prompt.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the prompt omitted a convention, the Grep finds no match. If the rewrite grew the study set past 1043, `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` fails reporting the new computed producer value.
demonstrations.seam: Not a behavior criterion. The budgets test calls `athena_cli::wiring::capabilities()` (exists) and compares with `athena_context::briefs::SYSTEM_FACTS`.

demonstrations.method: Run clippy on the whole workspace, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, after step 10's `cargo fmt --all`.
demonstrations.observes: Clippy finishes with no warnings and fmt --check exits 0 with no diff.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the added test helpers left an unused import or variable, a struct without a Debug derive (missing_debug_implementations = warn), a needless clone or unformatted lines, clippy would exit non-zero with the warning promoted to an error by -D warnings, and `cargo fmt --all --check` would print a diff and exit 1. So the pair fails on any lint or format fault in the new code in rules.rs, lib.rs and xtask/tests/policy.rs.
demonstrations.seam: The workspace's own tooling, run over the changed crates (athena-cap-study tests and xtask tests are compiled by --all-targets). No fake or fixture; tooling exists today.

demonstrations.method: Read CHANGELOG.md `## [Unreleased]` for a new bullet under `### Changed` covering the per-study validation, the prompt conventions, the new admission refusal and the boundary exemption. Run `git diff --stat` and `git status`.
demonstrations.observes: The changed files are only those in the plan's files list, none under studies/, not athena.toml and not docs/system-facts.md. The changelog bullet contains none of the boundary list's words.
demonstrations.fails_without: A missing changelog entry or a stray change under studies/firstmate-work-handling/ or athena.toml shows in the diff stat.
demonstrations.seam: Not a behavior criterion: git status/diff over the working copy.
